content: Blood pressure should be measured at every clinical visit for individuals diagnosed with diabetes. If an elevated blood pressure reading is observed, defined as a systolic pressure between 120–129 mmHg or a diastolic pressure below 80 mmHg, it is recommended to initiate regular monitoring of the patient’s blood pressure. Hypertension is diagnosed when the systolic blood pressure is equal to or exceeds 130 mmHg, or the diastolic blood pressure is equal to or exceeds 80 mmHg. This diagnosis must be confirmed through multiple blood pressure measurements to ensure accuracy.
